instruction: Compute the pass rate as the percentage of students scoring 30 or higher, rounded to two decimals, and record it in cell H10.

metadata.explanation: Task requires calculating the pass rate based on the grading scale (marks >= 30 means pass). Verified with Python by analyzing all 14 students: marks=[42, 94, 33, 6, 86, 67, 59, 60, 10, 85, 5, 73, 100, 32], passing students (marks >= 30)=11, total students=14, pass_rate=(11/14)*100=78.57142857142857% which rounds to 78.57%. Custom getter extracts the percentage value from cell H10, metric checks if it matches expected value within 0.01 tolerance.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement: checks cell H10 for the pass rate value
Getter logic is correct: extracts numeric value from cell H10 using openpyxl with data_only=True to get evaluated formula results
Metric logic is correct: compares result against expected value 78.57 with tolerance 0.01 for 2 decimal place rounding
Expected value is mathematically correct: 11 students passed (marks >= 30) out of 14 total = (11/14)*100 = 78.57%
Postconfig appropriately saves the file with Ctrl+S to ensure getter reads the latest cell value
Metric correctly handles expected parameter when type='rule': expected IS the rules dict {'value': 78.57}, so expected.get('value') correctly extracts 78.57
Complete semantic coverage: evaluator verifies the core requirement (correct value in correct cell)
